<Rep. Robert C. "Bobby" Scott, Rep. Joe Courtney, Rep. Frederica S. Wilson, Rep. Suzanne Bonamici, Rep. Mark DeSaulnier, Rep. Adelita S. Grijalva>: Finally, as with proposals to expand association health plans, H.R. 2571 threatens the stability of the broader insurance market. The ACA ensured a level playing field in the small group market by requiring insurers to use a single risk pool and comply with consumer protections such as coverage of Essential Health Benefits. However, self-insured, level-funded plans are not subject to that requirement, which risks segmenting the insurance market and--when healthier groups leave the single risk pool--disadvantages those left behind. As Families USA stated, ``level-funded plans not only pose risks to those families who rely on them for insurance, they can negatively impact families that access insurance in the traditional insurance markets by eroding risk pools.''\24\ The Center on Budget and Policy Priorities similarly warns that the policy changes included in this legislation would ``segment insurance markets.''\25\ When market segmentation occurs, older, sicker groups suffer, and health coverage becomes less affordable and potentially out of reach.\26\ As a result, H.R. 2571 threatens to raise costs throughout the broader health insurance market and could make it more difficult for certain groups to access affordable coverage.
\24\Id.
\25\Sarah Lueck, House Health Proposals Would Undermine Consumer Protections and Expand High-Income Tax Benefits, Ctr. on Budget & Pol'y Priorities (Jun. 5, 2023), https://www.cbpp.org/blog/house-health-proposals-would-undermine-consumer-protections-and-expand-high-income-tax.
\26\See, e.g., Am. Acad. of Actuaries, Drivers of 2020 Health Insurance Premium Changes (June 2019), https://www.actuary.org/sites/ default/files/2019-06/PremiumDrivers2020.pdf.
REPUBLICANS' AGENDA JEOPARDIZES HEALTH CARE FOR MILLIONS
H.R. 2571 is part of an ongoing effort by Congressional Republicans and the Trump Administration to roll back critical gains made under the ACA and the bill was considered by the Committee as part of a broader agenda that will harm the health and wellbeing of the American people. Specifically, on July 4, 2025, President Trump signed the ``Big, Ugly Law,''\27\ which rips health coverage away from approximately 10 million people.\28\ Moreover, the law's draconian cuts will squeeze state budgets and force additional cuts that will likely result in the scaling back of crucial benefits, disproportionately at the expense of home and community-based services for the elderly and people with disabilities.\29\ Additionally, these cuts will devastate hospitals and force many throughout the country to close--as the American Hospital Association warns, ``the bill will result in the curtailing of essential services and the closure of hospitals, particularly in rural areas.''\30\
\27\One Big Beautiful Bill Act, Pub. Law. No. 119-21 Sec. 70411
(2025).
\28\Cong. Budget Off., Estimate of Annual Changes in the Number of People Without Health Insurance Under Title VII, P.L. 119-21 (Aug. 11, 2025), https://www.cbo.gov/system/files/2025-08/61367-09Uninsured- Data.xlsx.
\29\The Arc, How Provider Taxes Fund Medicaid and Why Cuts Hurt People with Disabilities 2 (June 26, 2025), https://arceci.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/06/How-Provider-Taxes-Fund-Medicaid.pdf.
\30\Press Release, Am. Hosp. Ass'n, Statement of Rick Pollack President and CEO American Hospital Association (June 28, 2025), https://www.aha.org/press-releases/2025-06-28-aha-statement-senate-reconciliation-package.
Through their legislative and regulatory actions, Republicans have quietly--but aggressively--pushed closer than ever to their longstanding goal of repealing the ACA. The ``Big, Ugly Law'' will institute numerous harmful policy changes to deny ACA coverage to many while imposing additional bureaucratic hurdles on others, ultimately taking away Marketplace coverage from over 2 million people.\31\ Meanwhile, the Trump Administration has undermined the ACA through a draconian regulation issued by the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS).\32\ This Final Rule restricts coverage, raises costs, imposes paperwork requirements, and, by the Trump Administration's own estimates, will lead to up to 1.8 million people losing their coverage in 2026.\33\
\31\Cong. Budget Off., supra note 28.
\32\Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act; Marketplace Integrity and Affordability, 90 Fed. Reg. 27074, 27213 (June 25, 2025).
\33\Id. at 27215.
Moreover, Republicans are steering the American people toward unprecedented, devastating premium increases through their refusal to extend premium tax credits for millions of Americans. Under the American Rescue Plan Act (ARPA)\34\ and the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA),\35\ the ACA's advance premium tax credits were dramatically strengthened for millions, and the subsidy ``cliff'' for individuals earning over 400 percent of the Federal Poverty Level was entirely eliminated.\36\ As a result of these reforms, during the Open Enrollment Period for 2025, a record 24.3 million people signed up for coverage through Healthcare.gov and State-Based Marketplaces.\37\ However, Republicans have repeatedly refused to extend the tax credits prior to their expiration this year, which will result in nearly four million people losing health coverage\38\ and millions more Americans seeing their premiums, on average, more than double.\39\
\34\Pub. L. No. 117-2 (2021).
\35\Pub. L. No. 117-169 (2022).
\36\I.R.C. Sec. 36B.
\37\Jared Ortaliza et al., Enrollment Growth in the ACA Marketplaces, Kaiser Family Found. (Apr. 2, 2025), https://www.kff.org/ policy-watch/enrollment-growth-in-the-aca-marketplaces/.
\38\Cong. Budget Off., The Estimated Effects of Enacting Selected Health Coverage Policies on the Federal Budget and on the Number of People With Health Insurance (Sept. 18, 2025), https://www.cbo.gov/ publication/61734.
\39\Justin Lo et al., ACA Marketplace Premium Payments Would More than Double on Average Next Year if Enhanced Premium Tax Credits Expire, KFF (Sept. 30, 2025), https://www.kff.org/affordable-care-act/ aca-marketplace-premium-payments-would-more-than-double-on-average-next-year-if-enhanced-premium-tax-credits-expire/.
All told, this catastrophic Republican health agenda will rip coverage away from millions, slash the benefits of millions of low-income people and people with disabilities, and raise premiums and out-of-pocket costs for many millions more. The combined effect of the policies under this Republican health agenda has been estimated to result in the premature deaths of at least 51,000 people each year.\40\
\40\Letter from Rachel M. Wern et al. to Sen. Ron Wyden and Sen. Bernie Sanders (Jun. 3, 2025), https://ldi.upenn.edu/our-work/research-updates/research-memo-projected-mortality-impacts-of-the-budget-reconciliation-bill/.
CONCLUSION
For the reasons stated above, Committee Democrats unanimously opposed H.R. 2571 when the Committee on Education and Workforce considered it on June 25, 2025. We urge the House of Representatives to do the same.
Robert C. ``Bobby'' Scott,
Ranking Member.
Joe Courtney,
Frederica S. Wilson,
Suzanne Bonamici,
Mark DeSaulnier,
Adelita Grijalva,
Members of Congress.
